[edit | edit source]
In 2003, Massachusetts State Legislature designated the University of Massachusetts Amherst as a research university and the "flagship campus of the University of Massachusetts system".[30][31] The university was named a top producer of Fulbright Award winners in the 2008–2009 academic year. Additionally, in 2010, it was named one of the "Top Colleges and Universities Contributing to Teach For America's 2010 Teaching Corps."[32]
From World War II to 2023, the imagery on the official seal of the university was nearly identical to the state flag of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.[33] That image of the seal has been slowly removed starting in 2011, until March 2023 when a new image of the seal, featuring a profile of the Old Chapel spire, was ratified by the campus.[34]

There are approximately 1,300 full-time faculty at the university.[15] The university is organized into nine schools and colleges and offers 111 bachelor's degrees, 75 master's degrees, and 47 doctoral degrees.[15]

[edit | edit source]
UMass Amherst is part of the Five Colleges Consortium, which allows its students to attend classes, borrow books, work with professors, etc., at four other Pioneer Valley institutions: Amherst, Hampshire, Mount Holyoke, and Smith Colleges.
UMass Amherst holds the license for WFCR, the National Public Radio affiliate for Western Massachusetts. In 2014, the station moved its main operations to the Fuller Building on Main Street in Springfield, but retained some offices in Hampshire House on the UMass campus.[50]

value.text:
The University of Massachusetts Amherst (UMass Amherst) is a public land-grant research university in Amherst, Massachusetts, United States, and the flagship campus of the University of Massachusetts system. Founded on April 29, 1863, as Massachusetts Agricultural College under the federal Morrill Land-Grant Colleges Act, it initially provided instruction in agricultural, mechanical and military arts. Its first class of approximately 50 students entered in fall 1867. The institution became Massachusetts State College in 1931, a name used until 1947. In 2003, the Massachusetts legislature designated Amherst as a research university and the system’s flagship campus.

The university offers bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral degrees across fields including agriculture, engineering, natural sciences, computing, management, education, nursing, public health, humanities and social sciences. Through the Five College Consortium, its students can attend classes and use resources at Amherst, Hampshire, Mount Holyoke and Smith colleges. The Amherst campus lies mainly in Amherst and partly in neighboring Hadley. The Charles River Campus, acquired from the former Mount Ida College in 2018, provides additional instruction, residential facilities and professional development opportunities. A secondary instructional center also operates in Springfield. In fall 2025, UMass Amherst reported 31,318 students, comprising 24,019 undergraduates and 7,299 postgraduates.

On April 6, 2018, Mount Ida College announced that it would shut down and the University of Massachusetts would be absorbing its campus. Mount Ida students were given a guaranteed transfer to UMass Dartmouth, and the campus became part of UMass Amherst.[79]

Former names: Massachusetts Agricultural College (1863–1931)[1]Massachusetts State College (1931–1947)

The university was founded in 1863 under the provisions of the Federal Morrill Land-Grant Colleges Act to provide instruction to Massachusetts citizens in "agricultural, mechanical, and military arts."[19] Accordingly, the university was initially named the Massachusetts Agricultural College.[19] In 1867, the college had yet to admit any students and had not completed any buildings but had been through two presidents. That same year, William S. Clark was appointed president of the college and professor of botany.[20] He appointed a faculty, coordinated the completion of construction, and, in the fall of 1867, welcomed the first class of approximately 50 students. Clark became the first president to serve long-term after the school's opening.[21] Of the school's founding figures, there are a traditional "founding four" – Clark, Levi Stockbridge, Charles Goessmann, and Henry Hill Goodell.[22][23]

[edit | edit source]
In 2003, Massachusetts State Legislature designated the University of Massachusetts Amherst as a research university and the "flagship campus of the University of Massachusetts system".[30][31] The university was named a top producer of Fulbright Award winners in the 2008–2009 academic year. Additionally, in 2010, it was named one of the "Top Colleges and Universities Contributing to Teach For America's 2010 Teaching Corps."[32]
From World War II to 2023, the imagery on the official seal of the university was nearly identical to the state flag of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.[33] That image of the seal has been slowly removed starting in 2011, until March 2023 when a new image of the seal, featuring a profile of the Old Chapel spire, was ratified by the campus.[34]

There are approximately 1,300 full-time faculty at the university.[15] The university is organized into nine schools and colleges and offers 111 bachelor's degrees, 75 master's degrees, and 47 doctoral degrees.[15]

[edit | edit source]
UMass Amherst is part of the Five Colleges Consortium, which allows its students to attend classes, borrow books, work with professors, etc., at four other Pioneer Valley institutions: Amherst, Hampshire, Mount Holyoke, and Smith Colleges.
UMass Amherst holds the license for WFCR, the National Public Radio affiliate for Western Massachusetts. In 2014, the station moved its main operations to the Fuller Building on Main Street in Springfield, but retained some offices in Hampshire House on the UMass campus.[50]

value.text:
The University of Massachusetts Amherst (UMass Amherst) is a public land-grant research university in Amherst, Massachusetts, United States, and the flagship campus of the University of Massachusetts system. Founded on April 29, 1863, as Massachusetts Agricultural College under the federal Morrill Land-Grant Colleges Act, it initially provided instruction in agricultural, mechanical and military arts. Its first class of approximately 50 students entered in fall 1867. The institution became Massachusetts State College in 1931, a name used until 1947. In 2003, the Massachusetts legislature designated Amherst as a research university and the system’s flagship campus.

The university offers bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral degrees across fields including agriculture, engineering, natural sciences, computing, management, education, nursing, public health, humanities and social sciences. Through the Five College Consortium, its students can attend classes and use resources at Amherst, Hampshire, Mount Holyoke and Smith colleges. The Amherst campus lies mainly in Amherst and partly in neighboring Hadley. The Charles River Campus, acquired from the former Mount Ida College in 2018, provides additional instruction, residential facilities and professional development opportunities. A secondary instructional center also operates in Springfield. In fall 2025, UMass Amherst reported 31,318 students, comprising 24,019 undergraduates and 7,299 postgraduates.
